resources.string: Android build, under development: pick a target, scan the video, export the tracked video.
Pose benchmark — ONNX Runtime CPU / NPU
No .onnx model in the APK. CI exports yolov8s-pose and yolo11m-pose into assets; or copy .onnx files to Android/data/com.takipli.oynat/files/models/.
No photo picked: the bench uses a gray 1280x720 frame (decode cost is lower than with real people). Pick a photo with people for real numbers.
persons: %1$d\npre %2$s ms | infer %3$s ms | decode %4$s ms | total %5$s ms
mean %1$s | median %2$s | p95 %3$s ms (%4$s fps)\nmedian split: pre %5$s | infer %6$s | decode %7$s ms\npersons found: %8$d | thermal status: %9$d
Cancelled. The partial scan is saved; Scan / resume continues from it.
Tap the person or the body part to follow (on this first frame).
The scan keeps running with the screen off or the app closed; a notification shows progress and a Cancel button.
Done. Target: %1$s (%2$d samples). Views are saved; the preview and export come next.
Scan done (%1$d samples), but nobody was found at the tapped point. The scan is kept: pick again.
This scan has no target (nobody was at the tapped point). Go back and pick again.
Saved: views are in the scan file and in a .views.json next to it.
Exporting with the hardware encoder. Keep the app open and the screen on until it finishes.
Not enough free storage. Free some space and try again.
Not enough free storage for the export: about %1$d MB needed (the file is written twice while it is saved), %2$d MB free. Free some space and try again.
The pose model file is missing. Use a build that contains the .onnx models, or copy them to Android/data/com.takipli.oynat/files/models/.
The video cannot be read (moved, deleted, or access was lost). Go back and pick it again.
This phone cannot decode or encode this video format. Try H.264 instead of HEVC, or another clip.
Something went wrong. The details are in the error log (home screen, Share error log).
Battery is low and the phone is not charging. A long scan or export may be cut off: plug in the charger.

Personal-use build. Pose models: Ultralytics YOLOv8 / YOLO11 (AGPL-3.0), not for redistribution. ONNX Runtime (MIT), Qualcomm QNN runtime (Qualcomm terms), OpenCV, AndroidX Media3 and Compose (Apache-2.0). Details: THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md in the repository.
No person detected on this frame, so a scan will probably find nobody. Is the frame upright? Try another clip.
%1$d person(s) detected (boxes and skeletons shown). Tap the one to follow.
Draw around the object (e.g. both legs) with your finger; several strokes are allowed. The camera follows the whole drawn area.
The first frame black or unrelated to the rest of the video? Move to a frame where the target is visible, then pick it. Tracking runs both ways in time from that frame.
Allow this app to install apps in the screen that opened, then press Install again.
Updates only install over a build signed with the same key (the signed release from GitHub Releases).
EdgeTAM benchmark — CPU vs NPU per graph
All five EdgeTAM graphs are in the APK: scans use the memory tracker.
Memory graphs missing (sam-decoder-trk, sam-memenc, sam-memattn): scans use the prompt-per-frame tracker. Re-run the CI export.
EdgeTAM bench failed (see the error log on the home screen).
No photo picked: accuracy is compared on a gray frame with a bright disc. Pick a photo above for a realistic comparison.
What do you want to follow?
Tap the object you want to follow.
Getting smart select ready (a few seconds) …
Selected (the coloured area). Tap somewhere else to change it.
Nothing found there. Tap the middle of the object, or draw around it.
Tap the spot you want to follow. Smart object select is not in this app version, so the spot is followed with simple motion tracking.
Smart object tracking: ready (basic, the memory part is missing)
Smart object tracking: not in this app version (objects use simple motion tracking)
